title: Lola Young Announces 2027 Everything Begins Tour
excerpt: Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run scheduled for spring 2027 and her first full tour of the region since she cleared her live calendar in 2025.
body:
Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run scheduled for spring 2027 and her first full tour of the region since she cleared her live calendar in 2025. The route opens in Nashville on April 6 and closes in Los Angeles on May 4, with dates across the United States and Canada in between. Tickets go on general sale October 9 at 10 a.m. local time. The announcement puts a full headline schedule back on her calendar after more than a year in which live work returned carefully rather than all at once.

That pause began after Young collapsed during her set at All Things Go in New York in September 2025. A few days later, she cancelled every upcoming performance for the foreseeable future, including a North American tour that had been due to follow *I'm Only F**king Myself*. Her message at the time was unusually direct. She said she needed time to work on herself and asked fans to give her a second chance when she was ready to return. In December, her first substantial public update sounded deliberately cautious, saying she hoped to get back to performing gradually during 2026 rather than naming a date for a full comeback.

That gradual return became visible over the following months. "Messy" won Best Pop Solo Performance at the Grammys in February, where Young also performed, and she later resumed headline shows in the UK before moving back onto festival stages. By September she was back at All Things Go, roughly a year after the New York performance that had brought the previous run to an abrupt stop. The difference was not simply that she was performing again. She had spent most of 2026 testing a live schedule in pieces before committing to another long North American itinerary.

Her music changed alongside that return. "From Down Here," released in May and made with James Blake, was written after inspiration hit the day following the Grammys. Young described the song as being about missing an old high while knowing that a more grounded life is safer and ultimately more rewarding. That tension gives the track a calmer perspective than much of *I'm Only F**king Myself*, without sanding away the bluntness that made songs such as "Messy" connect in the first place. It also gives the next tour fresh material that belongs to the period after her break rather than to the album cycle that was interrupted by it.

The title Everything Begins comes from a reversal of Young's "Everything Ends" tattoo, but the phrase now has a fairly literal context around it. When she cancelled the 2025 dates, she did not announce a rescheduled tour or offer a timetable for returning. The months that followed were built around individual appearances, a Grammy performance, a handful of headline shows and festival sets. The 2027 run is different because it restores the kind of sustained schedule she had stepped away from. A year ago, Young was asking for time before anyone expected her back on the road. This time, she has put 17 dates on the calendar herself.
